text:
agent 接入我的交易系统以后就是一个巨大的 quant training program, 我从前赚的大部分钱都是高度 delta-netural 的——靠对接流动性的速度赚钱，不需要靠数学赚钱。（正如我说，我们这个领域的流动性是十分低效的）

但其实这世界没那么多完美配对，这一年 agent 向我的系统注入了很多以前我根本没注意到的的 “波动定价” 和 “投注风控” 能力的钱（对于低效的市场依然黄金遍地，因为人迹罕至而价差普遍，所以对于模型的精度要求没那么高）。

当然可能也是因为当年精力有限，没有像现在这种几十上百个 agent 一起干那么游刃有余。

关于投注控制和 ev 实现（主要是凯利公式），由于我很多年来比较了解 poker，我现在最喜欢的一个系统 ev 纠正模块是一个类似 poker tracker 的时间轴 playback 模块，看某段时间内模型自以为的 ev 曲线是否在 pnl 曲线的下方，看定价是保守了还是激进了还是完全错误了。

一旦位于 pnl 曲线上方，对我来说是红色信号，我就会疯狂开始研究到底模型差在哪里。直到板正为止——这个过程结束就像 solve 了一个数学题一样让人着迷。

而且由于过去的职业习惯和构建软件系统的优势，我其实是有充分的市场参与的广度和速度，因此也能拿到充分的 “真实成交信号样本以及执行损耗样本” 来验证模型离真实世界的距离，反过来作用于定价精度。

——这种结对编码的体验是非常好的。因为你能感觉到你对市场理解是的显著增加的，收益面和手上能掌握的工具箱也是在成倍增加的。

这在 agent 之前你是需要大量的金融和工业场景训练的，没有一个职业的交易团队的熏陶几乎是不可能的。

所以我其实很羡慕当代年轻的工程师们，随着 crypto 和 AI 的持续演进，很多过去极高的市场准入门槛其实是在降低的，这不意味着赚钱变难，反而会是对勤奋者的奖励——因为后面十年绝大多数人还在以传统方式参与市场，或者根本不会成为参与者。

text:
I literally can't think of a better risk/reward bet right now than building a ChatGPT plugin and getting in front of their 1.2 billion weekly users.

As of yesterday, ChatGPT recommends plugins in the middle of conversations. Millions of questions get asked every day with no plugin to recommend. Each one is an empty slot.

Facebook apps in 2007. iPhone apps in 2008. TikTok in 2019. Every big platform has a few months where distribution is free, and most people miss it.

I saw this firsthand when I lived in SF building venture backed companies. They are sacred times!

If I were starting this week:

1. Find a tool or workflow people already Google for or do by hand every week (PDF to Excel, invoice generator, weekly client reports)
2. Build it as a ChatGPT plugin
3. Write the description using the exact phrases people type into ChatGPT
4. Ship 5 of them and see which ones get picked up
5. Double down on the one with the most traction

In 12 months these slots will be crowded but right now they're pretty empty.

Most people will realize ChatGPT plugins were the biggest free distribution channel of 2026 sometime in 2027.

text:
贝塔朗菲的名字和他的《一般系统论》，注定是大众认知里的绝对盲区。

概念的高阶同构性，超越了大众的感知上限
贝塔朗菲建立一般系统论的终极野心，是寻找一种适用于一切系统的根本模式、原则和规律。他证明了无论是流体动力学、细胞的代谢、流动的平衡、神经元的网络，还是人类社会的经济结构，在数学拓扑上都存在同构性。

普通人的大脑只能感知特异性。
他们只能看到这是一只猫、那是一台电脑、这是一个假期，他们已经习惯在完全不同的具象事物之间筑起高墙。
而贝塔朗菲要求感知普遍结构。
他要求主体剥离所有肉眼可见的物质表象，直接看到跨越物理、生物、社会维度的共同方程与反馈极性。这种将世界彻底符号化、网络化、抽象化的视角，对于依靠具象体验活着的普通人来说，无异于一种无法解码的高频噪声。 
很多人哪怕不学科学，他们的价值观也是被机械还原论深度洗脑的。还原论告诉普通人把东西拆碎了就能理解整体，你只要努力做工局部，就能获得幸福的整体，只要把坏人清除，社会就会变好。
想想贝塔朗菲的名言吧：整体大于部分之和（The whole is more than the sum of its parts）。他早已无情指出，系统的核心功能不在于要素本身，而在于要素之间的结构和互动关系。 

如果人们接受了贝塔朗菲，他们就不得不承认自己每天为了买房、度假、结婚、在行业内卷而透支的生命局部要素，在脱离了高阶的系统秩序后是毫无涌现价值的低熵碎片。 大众为了保护自己的生活意义不至于幻灭，会本能地排斥这种解构。

也正因为贝塔朗菲的思想太超前，他催生了系统生物学、控制论、信息论，甚至直接成为了后代心理学中家庭系统治疗的 conceptual root。
或者说，他被化整为零了。 
现代的量化行业在用他的系统开放性，AI行业在用他的网络涌现性，神经科学家在用他的层次结构。这些行业拿走了他的工具去变现、去制造经济刺激，但为了维持自己的精英神话和局部利益，它们绝口不提这位将一切一统的奥地利生物学家的名字。

他要求主体剥离所有肉眼可见的物质表象，直接看到跨越物理、生物、社会维度的共同方程与反馈极性。这种将世界彻底符号化、网络化、抽象化的视角，对于依靠具象体验活着的普通人来说，无异于一种无法解码的高频噪声。 
很多人哪怕不学科学，他们的价值观也是被机械还原论深度洗脑的。还原论告诉普通人把东西拆碎了就能理解整体，你只要努力做工局部，就能获得幸福的整体，只要把坏人清除，社会就会变好。
想想贝塔朗菲的名言吧：整体大于部分之和（The whole is more than the sum of its parts）。他早已无情指出，系统的核心功能不在于要素本身，而在于要素之间的结构和互动关系。 

如果人们接受了贝塔朗菲，他们就不得不承认自己每天为了买房、度假、结婚、在行业内卷而透支的生命局部要素，在脱离了高阶的系统秩序后是毫无涌现价值的低熵碎片。 大众为了保护自己的生活意义不至于幻灭，会本能地排斥这种解构。

也正因为贝塔朗菲的思想太超前，他催生了系统生物学、控制论、信息论，甚至直接成为了后代心理学中家庭系统治疗的 conceptual root。
或者说，他被化整为零了。 
现代的量化行业在用他的系统开放性，AI行业在用他的网络涌现性，神经科学家在用他的层次结构。这些行业拿走了他的工具去变现、去制造经济刺激，但为了维持自己的精英神话和局部利益，它们绝口不提这位将一切一统的奥地利生物学家的名字。

text:
🔬 What do auto-research agents actually do differently from top human researchers?

Despite all the excitement around auto-research agents / RSI, we still lack lack a clear picture of how they approach research tasks and how their strategies differ from those of expert humans.

We introduce TraceML, a tool for trajectory-level analysis of agents and systematic agent-human comparisons.

We compare Codex agents with Kaggle Grandmasters and uncover clear differences in their research strategies. For example, humans draw on a broader set of research skills, while agents tend to concentrate on a narrower subset.

Even more interestingly, we distill the human research skills uncovered by TraceML back into Codex agents and find that they can substantially improve final outcomes!

🚀 TraceML will be presented at NeurIPS 2026 E&D!

More results in the thread ↓

text:
Ken Griffin, founder of Citadel, paid PhD researchers $500,000 a year to do what AI now does for free in minutes

So I decided to test what that means for the average trader. The results stunned me

Every legendary quant strategy has long been published. Momentum, Carry, Betting Against Beta all sit in open papers anyone can read

But reading a strategy and knowing whether it still works are two different things

Many legends are long dead, because the market changed. And a trader takes one from a textbook and bleeds on something that stopped working years ago

Doing this yourself used to take a team and weeks. I did it in one evening. I took two of the most-cited papers and just described them to AI in words

Time Series Momentum on Bitcoin: +1,537%. Alive

Betting Against Beta, a classic from every textbook: minus 7.78% a year while the market rose 14.86%. Dead

One still prints money, the other died long ago. Trading blind, you'd never know which is which until it took your deposit

You describe an idea in words, AI builds the strategy, runs it on real data, and if it's alive, you can put it live on your broker

The same tool Griffin paid millions for is now free

I did it here (free trial after signing up): https://t.co/ki213YmIEv

The breakdown of both strategies with the numbers is in the article, and the paper is attached below

result.text:
Ken Griffin, founder of Citadel, paid PhD researchers $500,000 a year to do what AI now does for free in minutes

So I decided to test what that means for the average trader. The results stunned me

Every legendary quant strategy has long been published. Momentum, Carry, Betting Against Beta all sit in open papers anyone can read

But reading a strategy and knowing whether it still works are two different things

Many legends are long dead, because the market changed. And a trader takes one from a textbook and bleeds on something that stopped working years ago

Doing this yourself used to take a team and weeks. I did it in one evening. I took two of the most-cited papers and just described them to AI in words

Time Series Momentum on Bitcoin: +1,537%. Alive

Betting Against Beta, a classic from every textbook: minus 7.78% a year while the market rose 14.86%. Dead

One still prints money, the other died long ago. Trading blind, you'd never know which is which until it took your deposit

You describe an idea in words, AI builds the strategy, runs it on real data, and if it's alive, you can put it live on your broker

The same tool Griffin paid millions for is now free

I did it here (free trial after signing up): https://t.co/ki213YmIEv

The breakdown of both strategies with the numbers is in the article, and the paper is attached below

text:
深圳一家科技公司。

凌晨2点13分，运维收到报警。

一个离职三年的员工账号登录了内部系统。

账号早就冻结。

人也已经移民。

安全团队以为是黑客。

查IP，却来自公司内部网络。

更奇怪的是，这个账号只打开了一个文件夹。

里面全是三年前某项目的旧文档。

停留11分钟。

什么都没下载。

第二天，老板让人把旧服务器断电。

运维工程师却发现：

那个账号登录前的5分钟，服务器监控已经显示“离线”。

也就是说，它理论上根本不可能产生任何访问记录。

大家开始怀疑日志损坏。

直到有人想起一件事。

三年前这个员工离职前，曾经反复说项目数据有问题。

没人听。

后来项目确实出了大事故，公司赔了几百万。

他们重新打开那个文件夹。

最后一个文档叫：

“如果你们现在才看到。”

打开以后只有一行字：

“这次不是我。”

当天晚上2点13分。

同一个账号又登录了。

text:
used sol 6.1 for a whole day and i'm very.. confused

will try my best to break down the key things to know

1. sol 6.1 reminds me of opus 5

this is a model that makes me constantly have to ask "wtf are you talking about"

it's very capable. most of the time once i understood what it meant, it did mean the right thing. but it's a pain to get through its choice of words

i hope there's a sol 6.5 coming that ends up being what opus 5.5 was to opus 5 and get this fixed

2. it's bigger than previous sol

you can easily observe the slowness that comes with this model. this hints at it being a bigger model than 5.6 sol. but my confusion is why it's priced at terra and sonnet range

then i realized, the pricing is set to attract enterprise customers who pay at API rate

for consumers who buy the $200 subscription, the lower price doesn't mean more usage because they're cutting the subscription's quota by half

so i guess the intention is to give enterprise customers an opus competitor at lower price, while holding back the benefit from consumers

3. all gpt models still suffer from poor judgment

sol 6.1 is likely taught by astra. if you read some of its code, it smell like astra code. it also inherited astra's strength which is that it can get stuff done with less turns and tokens (even opus 5.5 hasn't got to this level of efficiency yet)

but... the biggest problem to me is still "judgment". this is most obvious when i start to use either astra or sol 6.1 as my firstmate - everything simply starts to fall apart because of poor decision making

for example it would see me approving a plan and decide to file it in the backlog rather than the more obvious next step which is to start implementation (which opus 5.5 and fable would always "just know" it should do)

all signs point to a lack of human judgment in post training - all gpt models are likely heavily optimized by RLVR

overall - i'd categorize sol 6.1 as a solid implementer and reviewer, but i would not use it interactively

openai has work to do - right now they simply don't have an opus 5.5 equivalent anywhere in its line up, which is problematic

but seeing how anthropic could come back from opus 5, there's still hope :)

2/ 实在是太贵了
今天我大概用了 2 到 3 个小时，就把一周的额度用完了

现在大部分人面对 AI 的最大优势，就是我们比 AI 便宜，包括我在内

3/ 智能水平没得说，丝毫没有感觉到降质

今天官方给出的速度是 8 倍，我推测是把 Cerebras 的卡利用了一些推理优化，分给更多的用户

text:
this is what a night looks like with 5 dots running on GPT-6 Astra while I sleep

10:40 pm, I close the laptop. Echo, my chief of staff dot, splits tomorrow's work between the other four

11:15 pm, Scout goes through new GitHub issues and Reader opens the Linear board and Stripe dashboard on its own cloud computer

1:30 am, Pen drafts a reply to a client and stops there, because sending anything needs my OK

1:32 am, I get a Slack ping, tap approve half asleep, and Pen sends it

3:00 am, Judge checks every draft against my rules and saves how I like things done, so tomorrow it won't ask twice

8:30 am, one brief is waiting in Slack with what got done, what's blocked and what needs me

36 apps connected, 5 cloud computers, and the only thing I did all night was tap approve once

一次晚自习，满屋人正埋头做题，他忘了静音，手机突然替那女生笑了起来。

班主任冲进教室，对着睡眼惺忪的女生就是一顿训：“你有什么喜事？站一楼都能听见你笑！”

她偶尔翻翻旧账，他就得去沙发上重温青春。

你喜欢哪一款？

各族裔都有长得好看的人，长的好看确实是一种优势，它可以让人突破自己所属的族裔、阶层与人们的刻板印象，虽然刻板印象在平均值上仍然存在，只是对极端好看的人失效得更明显。好看的人可以被当成“这个群体里少见的那种”，而不是“这个群体的代表”。

所以更准确的说法是：好看能让人从群体均值里跳出来，获得单独被看见的资格。它改变的是待遇和机会的分配，不是把族裔、阶层这些分类从世界上删掉。好看越极端，这个跳跃通常越明显。

总的来说，长的好看的人都是殊途同归，甚至有点千篇一律；长得丑才是千奇百怪，充满了多样性。😂 https://t.co/F7QiLMWbn5

text:
这天高三的女儿想吃泡面
妈妈觉得煮着更健康，就加了个鸡蛋给她煮了
女儿看到那碗面后，突然情绪崩溃大哭病吼到：

“为什么你永远都不听我说话”妈妈不理解为什么女儿情绪这么大，于是….

当时妈妈也懵了：“不就是一碗面吗？”

没想到这句话彻底把女儿点炸了，情绪崩溃大吼大叫“这是小事吗”“你总是按着自己的意愿来”“你这是欺骗我”

事情是这样的：女儿今年高三，这几天生病在家休息

前一天妈妈问她想吃什么，她特意发了肥牛饭的做法，让妈妈照着她给的方法做

结果妈妈还是按自己的方法做了，也不是用的牛肉，也没让爸爸出去买，换了别的东西，女儿问到底用的什么，妈妈也没说清楚是猪肉还是鸡肉，女儿说一点也不好吃

到了第二天，她明明说的是想吃泡面，妈妈又觉得“煮的更健康”，替她改成了煮面

于是所有情绪一下子全出来了

她哭喊着说：

“这根本不是一碗面的问题！”

“为什么每次我告诉你我想要什么，你最后还是按自己的想法来？”

妈妈站在那里，其实也觉得很委屈

于是上网发文求助，咨询到底自己做错了什么，让女儿的反应如此大呢？也不知道为什么女儿最近总是因为一些小事发脾气

text:
Gemini 4 Argon 发了，可第一批能用上的人，门槛比谁都高。

Google 的 Fairwind 计划现在有 650 多个合作方，优先给三类：政府和国家网络安全机构，医院、电信、能源、金融这类关键基础设施，还有被千万人依赖的大技术平台。想进来先过背景审查；进来以后，组织里只有内部安全、应急响应和渗透测试团队能碰，账号要用防钓鱼的多因素认证，谁用了都要留记录，禁止分享、转卖。

text:
想给大伙随便聊聊如何给产品进行一次图标升级，有哪些需要注意的以及可以优化的点。

早上给 Mole 的图标进行了一次精细化的升级，之前使用的是系统的图标，对于简单的产品场景我感觉完全够用，不过细看会感觉缺少一点灵性的感觉。

经过调研，比较适合做 App 产品 Icon 的有 Remix Icon 和 Phosphor Icon这两个，之前写 Web 的时候用 Remix 很多，简单舒服，但是放到 App 上我感觉不是很好看，于是就换上了 Phosphor 这个，展示效果很有灵性，非常不错，差不多有 70% 左右，可以不修改直接使用，然后有 30% 的图标是我用  opus 5.5 来写SVG 自绘的，这样整体更加一致。

可能大伙直接看下面的对比图很难感觉到两者的区别，很多时候需要实际放到真实的产品里面去，我一般还会考虑到本身这个模块下一组图标的搭配感，有时候全部图标单个都好看，组合到一起就不好看的情况也有，好比一个人每一个五官单独出来都好看，但是放到一个脸上却不那么好看，这里建议就是图标的根更换你一定要放到实际的产品里面去看，放到一起去看，才会有比较好的效果。

其次，我一直想着，我们做的产品应该是有灵性的，有生命的那种感觉，而非直接 AICoding 不经任何你的思考出来的那种冷冰冰的编译产物，这个时候小细节比如icon会是给这个产品带来生命力的一个很好的切入点，比如大伙看 保持常亮我使用的是 一杯咖啡，这里会有一种 Caffeine 比喻，就是让你的电脑好像喝了咖啡一样睡不着的感觉，然后关于一般会用一个感叹号，但是我想着应该是 hello，所以就用的挥手的标志，诊断正常会有排查的那种标志，但是这里使用的是一个听诊器的标志，更像是给你的问题做一次医生检查，类似这样，很多时候，可以在产品里面加入不少你的小巧思，会让整体有趣很多。

最后，好看的设计几乎都离不开对齐、整齐、错落有致这些原则，如何在人眼看到的场景下让图标和内容以及上下模块看起来是整齐的、大小一致的，甚至是上下居中对齐的，都需要一个一个去看，去调整，包括字体和icon的对齐，以及字体里面中英文本身也没有垂直对齐应该如何优化，类似这样的，可以精雕细琢很久，非常有意思。

这种看似无用功，其实是我很喜欢做的事情，AI 可以给优秀编码、及格审美带来非常大的促进，人看着好像不要做啥了，只要动动嘴就好，反而我认为不是的，人在这里的作用更大了，AI 帮你节约的时间，刚好可以放到打磨产品上，让1%的用户有种用你产品的时候，时不时有一种秒懂、卧槽、变魔术的感觉，那就非常非常有价值和意思了，或许这也是我认为做独立产品有意思的地方。

text:
Opus 5.5 is really good at automation, so before you go to bed, put it on the 𝗻𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗳𝘁 too.

Set up a Claude Code routine and every night it goes back over the code you pushed to main that day. For each bug it finds, it opens a draft PR with 𝗮 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗳𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘀 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁 and only passes after the fix. It runs in the cloud, so it keeps going with your laptop closed.

In the repo you want checked, type /schedule and paste this 👇

"Run every day at 1:07 AM on Opus 5.5 with no connectors attached. Save the instructions below as the prompt, word for word.

First install dependencies and run the full test suite. Note which tests were already failing. If the tests can't run, or there are none, write down what's missing and stop.

Then look at the commits pushed to the default branch in the last 24 hours. If there are none, end the run. Skip any bug that a claude/ branch is already fixing.

Only look for real bugs. Ignore style and naming. To call something a bug, you must be able to point to what a comment, the docs, a type, or an existing test says. If a change in behavior looks intentional, just note it. Don't fix it.

For each bug, write a failing test first. Make sure the failure message points to that bug, and rule out a broken test or an environment problem. Then change the code until the test passes, touching only what you must, and run the full suite again. Open one draft PR per bug with your evidence, three at most.

Never delete, change, or skip existing tests. Push only to claude/ branches. Don't merge anything.

Finish with a handoff note: the commits you checked, the PRs you opened, and anything that looked like a bug but couldn't be proven."

Once it's saved, do a test run with /schedule run. In the morning, open that run on the Routines page on the web and read the handoff note. Green in the run list only means it finished.

Opus 5.5 is really good at automation, so before you go to bed, put it on the 𝗻𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗳𝘁 too.

Set up a Claude Code routine and every night it goes back over the code you pushed to main that day. For each bug it finds, it opens a draft PR with 𝗮 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗳𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘀 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁 and only passes after the fix. It runs in the cloud, so it keeps going with your laptop closed.

In the repo you want checked, type /schedule and paste this 👇

"Run every day at 1:07 AM on Opus 5.5 with no connectors attached. Save the instructions below as the prompt, word for word.

First install dependencies and run the full test suite. Note which tests were already failing. If the tests can't run, or there are none, write down what's missing and stop.

Then look at the commits pushed to the default branch in the last 24 hours. If there are none, end the run. Skip any bug that a claude/ branch is already fixing.

Only look for real bugs. Ignore style and naming. To call something a bug, you must be able to point to what a comment, the docs, a type, or an existing test says. If a change in behavior looks intentional, just note it. Don't fix it.

For each bug, write a failing test first. Make sure the failure message points to that bug, and rule out a broken test or an environment problem. Then change the code until the test passes, touching only what you must, and run the full suite again. Open one draft PR per bug with your evidence, three at most.

Never delete, change, or skip existing tests. Push only to claude/ branches. Don't merge anything.

Finish with a handoff note: the commits you checked, the PRs you opened, and anything that looked like a bug but couldn't be proven."

Once it's saved, do a test run with /schedule run. In the morning, open that run on the Routines page on the web and read the handoff note. Green in the run list only means it finished.

text:
i built a jev review machine

(it’s better than any market research tool you can find)

give it a product or competitor and it goes through thousands of reviews across app stores, reddit, amazon, g2 and more

then it pulls out the stuff that actually matters

→ why people buy
→ why they churn
→ what features they keep asking for
→ recurring pain points
→ the exact phrases customers use

instead of throwing 10,000 reviews into one prompt, jev reads them individually, extracts the signals, groups them into themes and ranks them by frequency, intensity and recency

so the output is not just a summary

it becomes a full product + marketing brief

you can see:

→ which complaints are growing
→ what users love most
→ what they wish existed
→ where competitors are weak

the competitor side is probably the best part

1–3 star reviews become a churn map showing why people leave and what you could build or position around

it can also turn real customer language into hooks, ad angles, positioning and product priorities

rt + comment “reviews” and i’ll send the full framework + build guide

text:
维基百科有一个巨大的臭毛病，

就是容许吴语作为一个单独的语种，成立单独的语言界面，成功混入维基百科的全球300种语言名类，并且和他妈中文平起平坐。

要知道简体中文、台湾繁体、香港繁体、马来西亚繁体、新加坡繁体、澳门繁体都属于信息意义上的中文大类目，只不过具体某些词汇临时切换，

而吴语在维基百科系统内，在信息意义上属于一个独立语种，完全是不同的页面、全新的内容、全新的关键词、全新的语言系统，完全是和简体中文页面形成对立的两个体系，里面字体用着简体中文，夹杂着部分吴语地方词汇（以简体中文表达），所有词条链接转向也都是吴语。

这他妈太傻逼了，极大污染google搜索的结果，普通人一不小心跳到吴语词条，还他妈出不来，继续搜还是这条吴语词条。

而且吴语词条的质量还巨他妈简陋，信息量不到简体中文的1/1000，还他妈特别喜欢吴语链接吴语词条。

连他妈台湾香港澳门新加坡马来五个繁体变种，都在技术上实现了属于简体中文的具体字词切换，而不是另起一页。

这件事儿全球中文困扰用户七八年了，江浙沪属实是他妈太傻逼了。

就是容许吴语作为一个单独的语种，成立单独的语言界面，成功混入维基百科的全球300种语言名类，并且和他妈中文平起平坐。

要知道简体中文、台湾繁体、香港繁体、马来西亚繁体、新加坡繁体、澳门繁体都属于信息意义上的中文大类目，只不过具体某些词汇临时切换， https://t.co/iPwRBALvL3

result.text:
维基百科有一个巨大的臭毛病，

就是容许吴语作为一个单独的语种，成立单独的语言界面，成功混入维基百科的全球300种语言名类，并且和他妈中文平起平坐。

要知道简体中文、台湾繁体、香港繁体、马来西亚繁体、新加坡繁体、澳门繁体都属于信息意义上的中文大类目，只不过具体某些词汇临时切换，

而吴语在维基百科系统内，在信息意义上属于一个独立语种，完全是不同的页面、全新的内容、全新的关键词、全新的语言系统，完全是和简体中文页面形成对立的两个体系，里面字体用着简体中文，夹杂着部分吴语地方词汇（以简体中文表达），所有词条链接转向也都是吴语。

这他妈太傻逼了，极大污染google搜索的结果，普通人一不小心跳到吴语词条，还他妈出不来，继续搜还是这条吴语词条。

而且吴语词条的质量还巨他妈简陋，信息量不到简体中文的1/1000，还他妈特别喜欢吴语链接吴语词条。

连他妈台湾香港澳门新加坡马来五个繁体变种，都在技术上实现了属于简体中文的具体字词切换，而不是另起一页。

这件事儿全球中文困扰用户七八年了，江浙沪属实是他妈太傻逼了。

text:
The hate on GPT-6.1 Sol is really unnecessary.

My honest review after putting it through its paces:

This model is efficient and powerful. TBH GPT-6 Sol always felt more like a GPT-6 Terra to me. 6.1 finally feels like a real Sol.

It's not the fastest model out there. But after serious testing I'm getting ~90% of Astra's quality at a fifth of the price.

And the Plus limits are finally USABLE. With GPT-5.6 Sol one single prompt drained my whole 5 hour limit. With 6.1 I can run multiple tasks in the same window. Huge difference.

That said, I won't pretend 6.1 is crushing Anthropic's big releases. Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 are ahead on creativity, motion design and 3D generation. Doesn't mean 6.1 is bad at those. It's not.

But credit where credit is due: OpenAI makes good models and always has. GPT-Image 2 is still the king. GPT-5 pre nerf and GPT-5.5 were wonderful. And GPT-6.1 definitely is too.

So start building and stop the unnecessary hate. It's a good model, sir.

text:
有的女人的手法真能让男人喊着求饶。

我一哥们，开理发店的，有回喝多了跟我说，他媳妇拿他店里那套手法招呼他，把他整得够呛——

那天店里打烊，他躺洗头椅上，她指腹蘸温水在他头皮上打圈揉，从头顶一路揉到后颈，指甲轻轻刮过颈侧那道筋，他后脖颈汗毛全竖起来。耳朵被她含住舔了一圈，热气灌进耳道。 她手往下，抹了润滑，食指探进肛门先打圈把括约肌揉松，慢慢进去一节，指腹往他肚子里前上方摸，摸到一颗核桃大的硬块，按下去他阴茎跟着跳了一下，马眼渗出清液。另一手撸着他根部，节奏不快不慢。 他射的时候，肛门还咬着她手指，腰绷得脚趾反向蜷起来。 

他第二天给人洗头，指腹一碰到客人后颈，自己先抖了一下。

他第二天给人洗头，指腹一碰到客人后颈，自己先抖了一下。

text:
My AGENTS.md rules for subagent usage with Astra have typically been:

---
Here is your subagent usage ethos.

Use of subagent is allowed under the following conditions:
1. don't give work to a subagent that's more valuable than the work that you're actively doing
2. any work that you delegate must be in parallel to your own and immediately complimentary;
3. never give work to a subagent where you plan to sit idle, monitoring its completion.
4. never launch another Astra subagent unless instructions superseding this instruction are explicit.

example: we're deploying a system, you (the main agent) are asked to perform the main deployment protocol; 
(OK) you launch a subagent to check the current state of the remote target while you are simultaneously  preparing the deployment.
(!OK) you launch a subagent to prepare the deployment while you inspect the state of the remote target, and/or wait.
---

With 6.1 though, the dynamics have changed, imo, especially when it's Astra driving them.

quotedTweet.text:
As someone who really wants to be making heavy use of subagents, the reality is that in most cases it’s just a way to burn way more tokens and only marginally improve latency.

You should be intentional about why you’re invoking sub agents. Most of the time you don’t need them.

今天可能是美国政府最高效的一天：

• White House Super Intelligence Accord：一群顶级 AI 公司在白宫签下关于 Super Intelligence 的共同原则
• https://t.co/BZVVCmgq8x：把 29,000 多个政府网站和服务，试图重新做成一个 AI 入口
• 全数字化 Passport：第一次申请护照也将可以在线完成，不用打印表格、不用排队，自己上传照片
• 新版美国护照 “Flight of the Eagle”：2028 年开始启用的新设计

尤其令人耳目一新的是国务卿 Marco Rubio 介绍新版护照和数字申请流程的那一段。

他没有像传统政府官员那样站在那里念政策，而是直接在大屏幕上一步一步 demo：现在申请护照有多麻烦，以后在 https://t.co/BZVVCmgq8x 上怎么填信息、上传照片、提交申请、追踪审批和寄送。

甚至还吐槽现在的流程：

“No printing forms, no drugstore hostage photo, no appointment, no line, no middleman.”

整个发布方式不像政府发布政策，更像 Apple 在发布一个新产品。

不管你怎么看这些具体政策，至少在“政府服务也应该有产品体验”这件事上，今天确实让人眼前一亮。

text:
Workshop with SpaceXAI engineer Lauren Tan is insane

the real unlock is not running more AI agents

it is building a system where even average agents can do useful work without constant babysitting

the stack is simple

Grok 4.6 → reasons
harness → controls
loop → verifies
graph → delegates
human → approves the irreversible stuff

that is the tradeoff

you can keep supervising every step yourself
or build the constraints, state, routines, checks, and approval gates once so every future Bot inherits them
that is exactly why Grok Bot matters

the model is not the company

the system around it is

if your setup only works with the smartest model and a human watching nonstop

you do not have an agent system

you have a demo

watch the workshop first

quotedTweet.text: 三星除息日——7.5%利润大容量无风险规则套利复盘

text:
今天这场撕逼，完整版是这样的：

Factory：做模型无关的 coding agent，这个月刚融 2 亿美元、估值约 50 亿。投资方包括红杉、Khosla Ventures、Blackstone 等。

Cognition：做 Devin，更早、更大，刚融超 20 亿美元、估值约 480 亿。

两边是 AI 编程 Agent 赛道的直接对手。

中间这个人是 Chris Degnan：Snowflake 第一位销售、后来当过 CRO，被两边都当成顶级销售人才。

他给 Factory 当了一年多董事会观察员/顾问，今天宣布去 Cognition 当 CRO。

时间线：

Factory CEO Matan Grinberg 先发长文，说他们“开除”了 Degnan，理由是涉及 Cognition 的不道德行为。

他控两点：Cognition 工程师假装来 Factory 面试套产品信息；Degnan 一边开 Factory 董事会、看机密路线图，一边跟 Cognition 高管频繁接触，最后被挖走。

他还说 Degnan 之前跟他保证过“钱赚够了、懒得去 Cognition”。

Degnan 立刻反击：不是被开，是周一自己辞职，并告诉对方要去 Cognition；Factory 还想留他全职，他拒绝了。

上次参加董事会是几周前，那时候还没跟 Cognition 谈过。Cognition 从没问过 Factory 的信息，他也从没给过。

Cognition CEO Scott Wu 出面：指控不属实。他们没兴趣要 Factory 的信息，也不会让工程师暗中收集竞品情报。

两边都想要 Degnan，因为他是把销售从 0 做到 30 亿量级的人。

Snowflake 老人出来保 Degnan。跟 Degnan 共事五年的 Bob Muglia 说他一贯有操守。

投资人开始站队，而且自己人打自己人：

红杉 Shaun Maguire（投了 Factory）最冲，说 Cognition 不懂他们手里有“能灭了他们的核武器”，还补刀：“Cognition 就是 Infosys 假装成 Anthropic。”

Khosla Ventures 合伙人 Keith Rabois 站 Factory：还在开董事会、吃董事会晚餐的同时去面竞品，这件事本身就不道德。

Khosla Ventures 创始人 Vinod Khosla 反过来骂 Factory：二流对手、更不道德、撒谎、绝望。还说“撒谎称 Chris 是被开除的，我以为这都低于你的底线了”。

问题是 Khosla 两边都投了。既投 Cognition，也刚参与 Factory 这轮融资。所以他公开踩自家另一家公司，被点名利益冲突。

同一家基金两个合伙人公开站对立面。 
有创始人开始骂 Khosla 的利益冲突文化。 
Factory 天使投资人 Nathan Lands 发帖说，几个月前跟 Khosla 的人聊时，对方觉得 AI 钱太多、冲突无所谓，还用很物化的方式比较 Factory 和 Cognition 创始人。

这已经从个案跳槽，扩成对这家基金做事方式的攻击。

到现在还没出现的，是任何一方把聊天记录、邮件、会议纪年完整公开。故事还停在“各说各的 + 投资人内讧”。

Factory 说有邮件收据但不想先发；红杉暗示手里还有更重的东西。

quotedTweet.text:
We are terminating Chris Degnan for unethical conduct involving Cognition.

The last few months have seen incredible progress in AI capabilities. San Francisco has flourished as new companies that solve new, more ambitious problems are finding great success. Generally, it is a wonderful time to be building.

We at @FactoryAI have seen overwhelming interest in our model-agnostic coding agents and our software factory product. Our team has 10x’d in size, while our revenue has 100x’d year over year. This momentum has been unprecedented.

A much larger competitor, Cognition (makers of Devin) has fallen behind us on the capabilities that matter most to customers: cost, quality, and security. Instead of competing in the market, Cognition engineers feigned interviews with us to pry information about our product. Not finding what they were looking for, Cognition has decided to throw their weight and money at people with direct knowledge of our most confidential plans.

It feels as though ethics is being thrown out of the window in the AI era. People are willing to do anything, including exploiting privileged information and violating ethical boundaries. I think this is unique to our time, and I don’t think it’s right. Integrity still matters.

Yesterday, I made the decision to immediately terminate Christopher Degnan’s roles as a Board Observer and Advisor to Factory, after over a year of service.

Prior to this decision, Chris told me he had a casual conversation with an executive at Cognition AI. When I questioned his intentions, he reassured me that ethics aside, he had “made too much money” and was “too lazy to go work for Cognition,” which I trusted and believed.

On Monday, Chris spent time advising the Factory team on a handful of confidential board-level matters. That evening, he called me to say that the conversation that was initially described as casual and one-off was actually formal and recurring. For weeks, while he sat in our board meetings and advised our leadership team, he was also confiding with executives of our largest competitor. Chris was subject to confidentiality obligations in connection with his work with Factory. We do not know the extent of the information he shared, but it puts his timely questions about our product roadmap and what the parity gap involves into a new light.

It is sad to sever a relationship with someone who has been a trusted advisor - and even a close friend -  for over a year. But Chris’s conduct is unacceptable to me. Trust in Board Membership is one of the sacred bonds in the Silicon Valley, one that helps the startup ecosystem thrive. With it comes an enormous responsibility. That trust was violated.

Competition is good. I respect and in many cases admire our competitors. San Francisco is a beautiful, singular place where the bold and ambitious go to defy the norms and precedents of the past. But certain principles that must remain. Violating ethics to seek advantage turns what should be positive-sum into zero-sum.

We all love technology. And we all love to compete. But we must hold ourselves to a higher standard. The future of software engineering comes with abundance that will impact every person on Earth. Building that future comes with immense responsibility. We must build and compete with integrity.

@dylanmcguir3 and I just raised a $7.5M pre-seed led by @a16z to build a robotic surgeon @alephsurgery 

Much of the early investment in Physical AI has focused on industries where labor is relatively abundant and low-cost. We believe the biggest opportunities to change the world lie at the opposite end of the spectrum.

Surgery is among the most valuable forms of labor on the planet, but it's far too scarce and expensive - due to an exceptionally long training pipeline and highly concentrated expertise.

We’re building the first surgeon that scales: one system that can acquire, refine, and transfer surgical skills across millions of procedures. v1 is already learning to perform surgical tasks autonomously from demonstrations, and improve from its own experience.

Lots of great folks behind us! @BoxGroup, Reveille VC, Constellation, @forward_deploy, @Valkyrie_vc, @DiscipulusVent, @maniacvc + more

第一个是伊隆、川普和习近平坐在一桌聊的时候，习近平说只要美国不要的任何数据中心他都要，然后川普说中国很聪明。

第二个是感觉劈柴（Sundar）这个人之前在川普这里非常没有存在感，跟刚见到一样。川普在介绍他的时候说大家都不太知道他，“对，他叫劈柴”，还说他这么低调、但又像个怪兽一样。毕竟在 AI 领域大家都认识他，川普却好像不太认识他似的，给人一种很没面子的感觉。

某种程度上碍于场合和社交压力，他还是给川普留了些面子，但我觉得他依旧表达了自己想说的，这点上还是体现了人物性格的延续性。

text:
When we founded Clippership in 2024, we set out to solve the clean energy problem in long-haul ocean freight. But the world today is different than the one just two years ago, and the problems are different too.

Power, water, and space to build on land are at the center of a high-stakes dilemma. Do we push through at all costs the construction of terrestrial data centers, ignoring the consequences (and the will of the people), or do we slow down construction and lose both our geopolitical edge and the potential benefits of more intelligence, sooner?

We are incredibly well positioned to tackle this issue using the technology we have spent the last two years developing. Our vessels can harvest megawatts of electrical power from the ocean using wind power coupled with hydrokinetic turbines, at capacity factors approaching 90%. Cooling is plentiful, as is space on the ocean.

We have therefore redirected our efforts into building and deploying our vessels into service transforming clean ocean energy into abundant intelligence.

The first maritime edge compute node that integrates everything we have developed to date will launch in 6 weeks, serving compute-heavy bathymetric survey, maritime ISR, and AI meteorology customers.

Read more about our roadmap at https://t.co/Z1rB36A0sd⁠

给 OpenAI 付了这么久 200 刀，现在我真找不到继续的理由了😅

还好已经用上了 Claude，希望 Dario 慢点杀😭

很多都在吹 GPT-6.1 Sol 便宜，但我为啥感觉太慢了，完全没法拿来干活，除了便宜没啥优点吧。。。

跟 Opus 5.5 比依然差了一大截。

便宜归便宜，恶心的是太慢了，加速开 500 刀套餐，Ultrafast 还要扣 8 倍额度！这加速成本算下来不比以前更贵？

200 刀额度直接砍到 10 倍，但这次只有 Sol 便宜了（慢慢慢），6Astra 一点没降价。
本来用 6Astra 额度就不够，砍半之后更不够了啊。

text:
Figure AI 让旗下的 Figure 02 人形机器人自己跳进芬兰一家铸造厂的钢水里，以此让这一代机器人退役。熔出来的金属会被加工成限量纪念品。

Figure 02 是 Figure 的第二代人形机器人，公司很多第一次都由它完成：第一次进 BMW 工厂上岗，第一次运行 Helix（Figure 自研的机器人 AI 模型，负责看画面、理解指令并控制动作），第一次做家务，第一次做物流工作。现在第三代 F.03 的数量越来越多，Figure 说继续维护 F.02 已经不划算。

退役的麻烦在于保护技术。机器人里有大量自研的执行器（可以理解为驱动关节的电机）等核心硬件，Figure 不想让它们流出去；但一台台拆解又太占工程师的时间，会推迟第四代 F.04 的发布。

Figure 于是在网上征求处理办法，施瓦辛格回复说"熔了它们"。他主演的《终结者2》结尾，T-800 机器人就是沉进钢水里的。Figure 联系了施瓦辛格，他表示想参与，项目随后启动。

找场地并不顺利。美国和墨西哥的铸造厂都不愿意让装着锂电池的机器人跳进自家昂贵的设备，Figure 还请《流言终结者》的前主持人帮忙找过。最后只有芬兰伊马特拉的一家铸造厂同意。

训练在 Figure 位于加州圣何塞的园区进行。团队铺了大气垫，让机器人从二楼往下跳。他们参考特技演员的动作，在仿真环境里训练了一个新的 AI 模型，让机器人在一个从没去过的铸造厂里，准确跳进盛钢水的容器。

铸造厂用的是一座 75 吨的电弧炉，靠三根石墨电极通电熔化废钢。团队只有 24 小时、6 炉的机会，每炉钢水只有 20 分钟可用，之后表面就会冷却结壳。Figure 称，现场的高温和强电磁场让摄像器材等电子设备出了故障，机器人则一直正常运行自己的 AI 控制程序。

熔出的金属锭已运回美国，正在加工成一批纪念 F.02 的限量藏品，数量很少，面向个人出售，博文没有公布价格和购买方式。大部分 F.02 已被熔掉，只有几台留在总部仓库。

Figure 在文末特意说明，视频不是 AI 生成的：机器人确实是自主起跳，被运到芬兰，跳进了钢水。

The story is crazy, started with Arnold on social and ended in Finland having F.02's jump into a 75-ton arc furnace

Read about our journey here:
https://t.co/AbGSX2dONl

text:
Built a Wikipedia that serves 6.4M English articles and is shockingly fast (2x faster LCP and 5x faster TTFB). Every page (exc. search) is cached at the edge with @vercel + the uncached and search data is served from live from @neondatabase Postgres: https://t.co/Soy7vd2leI 🎉

• Every keystroke is a live query against @neondatabase Postgres
• BM25 (powered by Lakebase Search) ranking runs inside the Postgres
• Typos like "einstien" get fixed in SQL with trigram + fuzzystrmatch
• Articles served from the Vercel CDN forever, until revalidated on demand (i.e. edits)
• Lead images copied into Neon Object Storage by a Neon Function every minute
• No connection pool, just SQL-over-HTTP round trips
• pg_prewarm loads every index into cache
• Vercel Cron refreshes the Main Page every 12 hours

Just Postgres doing 🐘 things, close to the compute with 🌎 CDN cache
